I’m sorry again for the delay and I’m sorry I couldn’t be more helpful!

Josh

messages.subject: Update compare solutions
messages.body_plain:
Dear Dr. Baumeister, dear tidyLPA team,

concerning my e-mail from Friday I have now done some further calculations and also took a peek in the programming on Github.

The first small issue I found is that the models are specified differently for the compare solutions command compared to the estimate profiles and bootstrap LRT command. Namely, the model with varying variances and zero covariances is specified as VVI in estimate profiles and bootstrap LRT, but as EEE in the compare solutions command. Similarly, the model with equal variances and equal covariances is specified as EEE in estimate profiles and bootstrap LRT, but as VVI in the compare solutions command. Assuming that the labeling in estimate profiles and bootstrap LRT is correct, this code should do it for the compare solutions command:

model <- case_when(

variances == "equal" & covariances == "zero" ~ "EEI",

variances == "varying" & covariances == "zero" ~ "VVI",

variances == "equal" & covariances == "equal" ~ "EEE",

# variances == "varying" & covariances == "equal" ~ 4, # I'd remove

# variances == "equal" & covariances == "varying" ~ 5,

variances == "varying" & covariances == "varying" ~ "VVV"

)

Apart from this, some further calculations have shown that the BIC and Log Likelihood values I get by working with estimate profiles and bootstrap LRT and specifying a equal-equal model are the same as the equal-zero model in the plot of the compare solutions command. Same way round, equal-zero values calculated with estimate profiles and bootstrap LRT are the same as equal-equal in the plot of the compare solutions command. However, I could not identify what one should change within the code.

For carrying on with my data analyses (which are unfortunately sort of urgent as they are part of a review) it would be completely enough for now to know which commands calculate “correctly”. So, are the estimate profiles and bootstrap LRT correct in specifying the models or is the compare solutions command correct?

Thanks so much for your time and effort!

Fiona

Dear Fiona, thank you so much for your message about this and for diving into the code on GitHub. Yes, you are right – the models in compare_solution() are not correct. I double-checked (and checked what we wrote in the  vignette here <https://jrosen48.github.io/tidyLPA/articles/Introduction_to_tidyLPA.html>!) and the change you suggested is correct. Note that we just made some changes to this function that introduced this issue—and (I think) this was working correctly previously. In fact, we used to have tests that benchmarked each function to known output, but in the coruse of making changes to the interface to the function we removed them. We’ll be sure to plan to add them back in future versions so this doesn’t happen again.

I just made the change in the development version and pushed the changes to GitHub; devtools::install_github(“jrosen48/tidyLPA”) should include this change.

Thank you so much for pointing this out.

Sincerely,

Josh

Dear Dr. Baumeister, dear tidyLPA team,

concerning my e-mail from Friday I have now done some further calculations and also took a peek in the programming on Github.

The first small issue I found is that the models are specified differently for the compare solutions command compared to the estimate profiles and bootstrap LRT command. Namely, the model with varying variances and zero covariances is specified as VVI in estimate profiles and bootstrap LRT, but as EEE in the compare solutions command. Similarly, the model with equal variances and equal covariances is specified as EEE in estimate profiles and bootstrap LRT, but as VVI in the compare solutions command. Assuming that the labeling in estimate profiles and bootstrap LRT is correct, this code should do it for the compare solutions command:

model <- case_when(

variances == "equal" & covariances == "zero" ~ "EEI",

variances == "varying" & covariances == "zero" ~ "VVI",

variances == "equal" & covariances == "equal" ~ "EEE",

# variances == "varying" & covariances == "equal" ~ 4, # I'd remove

# variances == "equal" & covariances == "varying" ~ 5,

variances == "varying" & covariances == "varying" ~ "VVV"

)

Apart from this, some further calculations have shown that the BIC and Log Likelihood values I get by working with estimate profiles and bootstrap LRT and specifying a equal-equal model are the same as the equal-zero model in the plot of the compare solutions command. Same way round, equal-zero values calculated with estimate profiles and bootstrap LRT are the same as equal-equal in the plot of the compare solutions command. However, I could not identify what one should change within the code.

For carrying on with my data analyses (which are unfortunately sort of urgent as they are part of a review) it would be completely enough for now to know which commands calculate “correctly”. So, are the estimate profiles and bootstrap LRT correct in specifying the models or is the compare solutions command correct?

Thanks so much for your time and effort!
